title: SWCraft requirements interchange file
description: A Sphinx-Needs needs.json (format 1), as 'swcraft import requirements --source FILE' reads it with no --mapping: SWCraft's own names, and Sphinx-Needs' own keys allowed beside them. current_version selects one of versions; its name is the baseline (the empty name states none), and its needs are imported. This schema judges every version alike; SWCraft's reader validates the selected version alone, and checks every other one only to be an object whose needs is an object. Seven rules are checked by SWCraft's reader alone: a need's id equals the key it is filed under, needs_amount equals the number of needs, a non-empty current_version names a key of versions, no JSON object repeats a key, a need's id, each parent id and current_version hold no lone surrogate, a key ending in _back mirrors a key that is read or allowed, and each parent id follows the requirement id rule. Under a --mapping, this schema does not judge the file.

current_version.description: The name of the version to import; it becomes each imported requirement's baseline. The empty name is the Sphinx-Needs builder's for a project with no version, and states no baseline.

requirementId.description: A requirement id: not blank (the whitespace class is spelled out as in text), no '@' (a link's version separator), no ':' (an element reference), no '/', no '\' and no '..'.

text.description: Not blank: at least one character outside the whitespace class, which is spelled out code point by code point because Python's and ECMA-262's '\s' differ.

needs.description: The needs of this version, each filed under its own id.

needs_amount.description: The number of needs, when stated.

needs_schema.description: Not validated. SWCraft reads one fact of it: whether the derived_from property carries field_type "links", which makes each parent follow Sphinx-Needs' link grammar (the part and the condition dropped).

needs_defaults_removed.description: Only false: a file written with its defaults removed cannot tell an omitted key from an absent one.

need.description: A need: the keys SWCraft reads, typed; every key Sphinx-Needs 9.2.0 writes itself and any key ending in _back allowed with any value; any other key refused.

content.description: The requirement's text as written: Sphinx-Needs' raw directive body, markup included; it becomes the description.

status.description: Read and not stored; exactly "rejected" removes the requirement.

asil.description: The level allocated to the requirement; null, "" or absent allocates none.

document.description: The source document, as written; null, "" or absent states none.

revision.description: The source tool's own revision, as written; never read as a number; null, "" or absent states none.

derived_from.description: The parent requirements, each a non-blank string; a parent listed twice is one. Taken whole, unless the version's needs_schema labels derived_from as links: then a part (.p1) and a condition ([...]) are dropped. SWCraft's reader judges each resulting id by the requirement id rule.
